messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime Q&A 
maria: Collating kernel/batching/caching questions here. Drop follow-ups or request deep dives.
 david: thx. can you summarize which kernel change gives the biggest perf per token?
 raj: short: fused attention for short contexts and int8 matmul fast path. fused attention reduces compute + memory moves for chat-like loads. int8 wins on large matmuls but needs model-specific calibration.
 anne: does fused attention change output determinism? worried about tiny fp differences for evals.
 raj: there are small numerical diffs. we run regression evals on our canary and require metric parity thresholds (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR-style evals) before enabling the fast path for a model. users can pin variants.
 ops-bot: canary deploy: runtime/fused-attn -> canary-cluster at 2024-08-06T09:00Z
 carla: about batching: how often should teams tune batch_delay_ms vs leaving autoscaling?
 raj: defaults are safe. tune if you need sub-100ms p50 and can accept throughput loss. Lower batch_delay_ms favors latency (smaller batches), increasing token cost. For bursty traffic, priority lanes + lower batch_delay for interactive routes.
 david: any rule-of-thumb numbers? like batch_delay 5ms vs 20ms?
 raj: empirically: 5-10ms is good for human-interactive chat; 20-50ms for background generation. p50 improved by ~30-60% at 5ms vs 50ms in our traces, p99 less predictable.
 maria: caching: prefix vs KV cache — what should customers expect?
 carla: prefix cache returns cached responses end-to-end for repeated prompts (great for templates). KV cache reuse reduces compute for generation when continuation tokens share context. We expose both: route-level toggles and per-request cache control headers.
 anne: will Console show cache hit metrics and batch distributions?
 ops-bot: new metric created: runtime.batch.avg_size and runtime.cache.prefix_hit_rate added to per-route dashboards
 carla: yes we'll add dashboard templates and an alert for cache-hit drop > 30% vs baseline.
 david: rollout strategy question: if a kernel causes regressions for one customer, how fast can we rollback?
 raj: immediate per-model variant fallback + canary fleet rollback. we also support pinning a customer's Dedicated nodes to stable variants for 24-72h.
 maria: follow-up meetup? looks like kernel owners want to present microbenchmarks. propose a 45min tech deep dive next Tue.
 anne: +1. pls include example configs to reproduce perf numbers.
 carla: I'll prepare a short doc with tuning recipes (batch_delay, max_batch_tokens, priority flag) and sample load tests.
 maria: great. I'll add notes to the all-hands follow-up and share slides. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
